title: Route request
description: What the customer asks the router for, in one round: from where, to where, how much, for which objective, and the worst outcome accepted (REQ-QTE-11, REQ-ORD-27). The amount is what leaves the origin, and the direction is origin to destination. The request's id is also its decision record's id: one routing per request, so each round has its own id.

request_id.description: The request's id, and so its decision record's.

to.description: Where the value must arrive: the one destination and to asset (REQ-AUZ-3).

amount.description: The amount that leaves the origin, in its unit.

floor.description: The worst acceptable outcome: the least the customer accepts at the destination, in its unit (REQ-ORD-27). Absent if the customer set none.

follows.description: At a recalculation, the choice-round request whose decision record this one follows for the same order (SAD section 3).

round.description: Which round this routing is (REQ-CAT-5, DEC-8). A shortlist round runs over advertised figures and chooses nothing: the candidates it doesn't drop are the shortlist. A choice round runs over a snapshot that adds fresh quotes, dry-run and eligibility answers for the shortlisted providers only, and names the shortlist round it refines, so both are recorded (REQ-AUD-4). The choice round chooses only a candidate whose every operation is confirmed: it cites an accepted dry-run answer of its provider for its tuple, at its amount, within its validity and not void, which for a route or exchange is the provider's fresh quote and for a withdrawal or deposit the reserve's accepted dry run. Any other is dropped as unconfirmed. Checked by the contract's Rust types.

refines.description: The shortlist round this choice round refines: its request id, and its snapshot's taken_at. A confirming answer must be made at or after that time, checked by the contract's Rust types.

objective.description: What the router optimises for (REQ-QTE-11); a tagged object, so more can be added. lowest_total_cost, the default, wants the largest sum over the candidate's parts of the last operation's amount_out. fastest_settlement wants the smallest settlement time: a part's is the sum of its operations' declared settlement seconds, each from the fresh quote the operation cites or else its price, and a split's is its slowest part's. Candidates equal by the objective are ordered by candidate_id ascending, comparing bytes, and the first is chosen. Whoever builds the request writes the default when the customer chose none.
